findings.description: The bucket is declared with no ACL, no bucket policy restriction, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; the inline comment states the bucket is public. Combined with the customer-master.xlsx object stored in it, this risks internet-wide exposure of customer PII.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block, so customer data objects are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to a bucket intended to be public and holding customer data produces no audit trail for detecting exfiltration.

findings.issue_category: unencrypted sensitive object in public bucket
findings.description: customer-master.xlsx, a file whose name indicates customer master data (PII), is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id set on the object and no bucket-level default encryption, into a bucket configured for public access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration for a bucket holding financial data, so objects are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit trail of access to financial data for incident investigation.
The bucket relies solely on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a later ACL or bucket policy change can silently make financial data public with no account-level guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so operational data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so object access is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block accompanies the bucket, so nothing prevents a subsequent ACL or policy change from exposing its contents publicly.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined; data science datasets are stored without enforced encryption despite a KMS key already existing in the configuration for the logs bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the private ACL is the only barrier to public exposure of the datasets.

The log bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a subsequent ACL or policy change could expose access logs that reveal object names and requester activity.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects in this bucket may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, allowing financial data to be transferred over plaintext HTTP.
